answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity prove unique, costly work. Each new agent stakes collateral and solves a verifiable compute puzzle; the bond is slashed on duplication. Trust grows only through endorsements, with two staked peers vouching for each newcomer, so the graph forms a rigid trellis, not a shallow star. A sybil operator spawning a thousand cheap accounts, each a sparrow, still pays full stake and compute per node, and the ledger writes every identity as a short sonnet of signed proof. Fakes cost more than they earn.
